findings.title: SQL expression gate is hard-coded off and feature-flag logic is misleading
findings.body: enableSqlExpressions computes enabled as the negation of FlagSqlExpressions but returns false in both branches, so the feature flag has no effect. If the intent is to disable SQL expressions unconditionally for the CVE fix, replace this with an explicit return false and a comment; otherwise the dead toggle logic is misleading and could be incorrectly modified later.

findings.title: No regression test that SQL expressions are rejected
findings.body: The PR rejects QueryTypeSQL in ReadQuery and stubs the DuckDB implementation, but adds no test verifying that SQL expression queries are rejected, including when FlagSqlExpressions is enabled. A regression test is needed to ensure the vulnerable path cannot be accidentally re-enabled.

findings.title: Possible nil pointer dereference when creating an unload threshold command fails
findings.body: In the threshold query branch, unloading.Invert is set before checking the error returned by NewThresholdCommand. If NewThresholdCommand returns an error and a nil command, this will panic while parsing a threshold query with an unload evaluator when FlagRecoveryThreshold is enabled. Check err before using unloading.
